children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Shree Cement's consolidated net profit fell more than 15% year-on-year to 263 crore in September quarter, weighed down by higher fuel costs despite growth in sales volumes. This was third consecutive quarter in which the company reported a year-on-year decline in consolidated profit.

The country's third-largest cement producer by capacity recorded a 14% year-on-year increase in sales volume to 10.52 million tonnes during the quarter, while revenue from operations rose 24% to 5,897 crore. Consolidated earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose to 1,016 crore from 974 crore a year earlier. However, EBITDA per tonne of cement fell 8% year-on-year to 966 from 1,055, primarily due to elevated fuel costs. Consolidated power and fuel costs rose nearly 56% year-on-year to 1,843.2 crore.

title: Shree Cement Net Falls 15% on Higher Fuel Costs
